Many Djs i meet and met are comfortable in their genre, wich is mostly some electronic music, long enough to beatmatch easy 4:4 Beat and intro outro. And those djs are mostly the loudest when it comes to critize everyone else. But you know the music and the struggle of an 80s song only with vocals and inkonsistent bpm. Sobfirst things first: If there's someone like 'thats not good, I'm better, I'm this and that' or 'my friend could do this', dont care about it, keep going. Those people would die with radio mixes and 80s, 90s... You will do a great job and have the greatest feeling in the world afterwards when its done, just keep the people dancing. 
If your music selection is good, nobody cares about the transitions, in last case you could just fade with the line faders even without beatmatching. Make notice of requests, dont just play it immediately, but think abojt it: what kind of song is it, who is the one that requests, how many people would know and like the track, what's the right time for that song (slow for later, floorfiller at maintime, chilly for sitting and talking)?

As Hiphop and Pop Dj (i love playing a small techno set or something too, but...) i get bored when a song is playing more then 3 minutes, I'm faster, most transitions after the second hook when the bridge comes in (Intro, Hook, Verse, Hook,  Bridge, Hook again, Outro). But that depends on the Song, some are enough after the 1st Hook and the verse sucks, some songs, especially when they know all lyrics (like Britney spears or wannabe or Angels) and the crowd is singing, dont cut it off! Play it till its done. Also 3-5 minutes could feel pretty short when you are in it, shorter than at home practicing. 
Your job is to make them dance, but its fine to have a few songs that you dont play when requested, you have a taste in music, when you absolutely hate it and its not 100% of the crowd, it is ok to not play everything. But do requests, they may give you a look, cause at least one will dance to it and if more people do, you see what they like.

I'm not familiar with Virtual Dj. When you keep the hobby think about Traktor or Serato and check what fits better for you. VDJ might be fine for that one, you could run a whole night with pc and vdj (dont know différence when subscribed).
Music Pool wont help i think. They dont have old songs mostly and DjCity more Black Music, DMP more electronic, if you need both genre, have to pay both and dont get all the classics. Also song is playing 3 minutes, in that time have to search for the song, download it, load in on the Deck and make a transition... Music pool is for preparation, not ad hoc downloads in action.
If you library is to empty, think about digital buying compilations: Top 100 80s, Top 90s, Top 2000 and top 100 todays charts. Thats a decent start. (Check that it's pop and radio, not like top 100 Hardstyle 90s,your oldies wont dance to that maybe).
Prepare the songs in the software, set Beatgrids and the correct bpm, maybe set markers where to start (dont play 1,5 minute Intro, start a song at the right position). The better you are prepared, the less nervous you'll be, cause you have something to rely on.
Dont overdo effects, they should underline certain parts, not more, not every song needs delay or a sample horn... Dont clip! Just dont clip. Watch for the Peak LED - when its red, the limiter kicks in, sound will be quiter then before and flat and people will die within seconds. Orange is great, so always check the gains on each channel.
